title: PLA drone enters Pratas territorial airspace
detail: MND said a Chinese reconnaissance drone flew in Pratas (Dongsha) territorial airspace for several minutes around 5:44-5:48am at an altitude beyond air-defence range; Taiwan raised alert levels and broadcast radio warnings.
attribution: Ministry of National Defense via Taipei Times

title: Keelung apartment fire kills firefighter and resident
detail: A fire from a short-circuited intercom on Leli 3rd Street killed a woman and a firefighter squad leader who gave her his oxygen mask.
attribution: Keelung City Fire Department via Taipei Times

title: Bird flu confirmed at Fengyuan egg farm
detail: Highly pathogenic avian influenza confirmed at a Taichung egg farm after ~1,700 hens died; ~5,300 remaining birds to be culled; farmer faces up to NT$1 million fine for not reporting.
agency: Taichung Animal Protection and Health Inspection Office
attribution: Taichung Animal Protection and Health Inspection Office via Taipei Times

title: First measles cluster of 2026
detail: Taiwan CDC reported the year's first measles cluster with 526 contacts under monitoring.
attribution: Taiwan Centers for Disease Control via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: 62 indicted in Prince Group laundering case
detail: Taipei prosecutors indicted 62 people and 13 companies for laundering at least US$339 million into Taiwan for Cambodia-based Prince Group, founded by sanctioned tycoon Chen Zhi; about US$174 million in assets incl. 24 properties and 35 vehicles seized.
attribution: Taipei District Prosecutors Office via The Record (Recorded Future News)

title: Guangfu township chief indicted over 2025 barrier lake deaths
detail: Hualien prosecutors indicted Guangfu Township chief Lin Ching-shui for dereliction causing catastrophe and negligent manslaughter over evacuation failures in the 2025 Mataian barrier lake flood that killed 19.
attribution: Hualien District Prosecutors Office via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: Fire at Hsinchu extra-high-voltage substation kills 1
detail: Fire during equipment testing at Zhuyuan substation killed 1 and injured 2; brief voltage dip in Hsinchu Science Park, no outage.
attribution: Hsinchu City Fire Bureau via Taipei Times

title: 24 PLA aircraft cross Taiwan Strait median line
detail: MND reported 36 PLA aircraft sorties, 24 of which crossed the median line into northern, central, southwestern and eastern ADIZ, plus 8 naval vessels and 1 official ship, in the 24 hours to 6am.
attribution: Ministry of National Defense via Taipei Times

title: Ring laundered via credit-card prepayments and Macau casinos
detail: Yunlin prosecutors said 10 people laundered NT$278.3 billion using nominee accounts, credit-card prepayments and Macau casino chips; NT$258 million seized.
attribution: Yunlin District Prosecutors Office / CIB via Inside Asian Gaming

title: Two bodies found after Nangang factory fire
detail: Police said two bodies were found in a corrugated-metal factory that burned in the early hours in Taipei's Nangang District.
attribution: Police via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: Taiwan-Matsu No. 3 cable damaged
detail: Chunghwa Telecom reported fibre damage on the Dongyin-Beigan section, suspected from salvage operations by Chinese vessel Hai Hong Gong 66; MODA said communications unaffected; repairs expected by July.
agency: Chunghwa Telecom / Ministry of Digital Affairs
attribution: Chunghwa Telecom / Ministry of Digital Affairs via Taipei Times

title: Chinese salvage vessel captain detained over Matsu cable damage
detail: Coast Guard Administration halted salvage work and detained the captain of Chinese vessel Hai Hong Gong 66 after Chunghwa Telecom suspected its operations off Dongyin damaged the Taiwan-Matsu No. 3 cable; 11 crew questioned and case referred to Lienchiang prosecutors.
attribution: Coast Guard Administration via Taipei Times

title: Taiwan to bolster Pratas defences amid Chinese pressure
detail: Ocean Affairs Council Minister Kuan Bi-ling said Taiwan plans infrastructure upgrades and more capable vessels for the Pratas, citing increased Chinese government-boat activity and the January drone overflight.
attribution: Ocean Affairs Council via Taipei Times

title: Power faults delay Eastern Line on holiday weekend
detail: Two power faults took eastbound tracks out of service between Sandiaoling-Sijiaoting and Su'ao Xin-Dong'ao from ~1:50pm, forcing single-track working during Tomb Sweeping weekend.
attribution: Taiwan Railway Corporation via Taiwan News

title: M5.7 quake near Hualien City, strongest of year
detail: CWA recorded M5.7 at 1:14am about 5.4km NNE of Hualien County Hall, depth 17.5km, intensity 4; M4.8 aftershock at 5:23am; no casualties. (Taipei Times dated the report April 6; VolcanoDiscovery gives April 5 local time.)
attribution: Central Weather Administration via Taipei Times

title: Taiwan regains ASF-free status
detail: WOAH reinstated Taiwan's African swine fever-free status after a three-month disease-free period following the October 2025 Taichung outbreak.
agency: World Organisation for Animal Health / Ministry of Agriculture
attribution: World Organisation for Animal Health / Ministry of Agriculture via TaiwanPlus

title: 99 hospitalized in Xindian bento poisoning
detail: 99 people sought hospital care after eating boxed meals from a Xindian restaurant chain; three branches closed and sanitation violations found.
agency: New Taipei City Department of Health
attribution: New Taipei City Department of Health via Taiwan News

title: Carrier Liaoning transits Taiwan Strait
detail: MND said it monitored the Chinese aircraft carrier Liaoning passing through the Taiwan Strait and released a surveillance photo; it also reported 5 PLA aircraft and 12 vessels around Taiwan, 4 aircraft crossing the median line.
attribution: Ministry of National Defense via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: Rockfall damages Daqingshui Tunnel on Suhua Highway
detail: A nearly 3m rock damaged the tunnel roof at km 159.4 of Provincial Highway 9; tunnel closed temporarily for repairs then reopened with 24h monitoring.
attribution: Highway Bureau Eastern Region Branch via Taiwan News

title: Investigation Bureau busts NT$5.4bn gambling laundering ring
detail: MJIB said a ring used shell companies, virtual accounts and game-point payment codes plus a cash 'money house' to launder NT$5.4 billion; 9 held, 27 questioned, 2,184 USDT seized.
attribution: Investigation Bureau via Taiwan News

title: Dongyin cable breaks, microwave backup activated
detail: MODA activated microwave backup after the Dongyin-Beigan cable broke, apparently when bad weather shifted a shipwreck onto it; cable TV unavailable and minor internet delays for ~1,500 residents.
attribution: Ministry of Digital Affairs via Taipei Times

title: Four China Coast Guard ships enter Kinmen restricted waters
detail: CGA said four Chinese coast guard ships entered Kinmen restricted waters at 2:50pm and left at 5:03pm after radio warnings and shadowing; CGA called it gray-zone harassment following China's May 1 fishing moratorium.
attribution: Coast Guard Administration via Taiwan News

title: 16 arrested over charity-themed investment scam
detail: New Taipei police arrested 16 in a ring using Facebook ads and Line groups for fake investment funds, defrauding over NT$140 million; donation certificates reused by overseas scam centres.
agency: New Taipei City Police Criminal Investigation Corps
attribution: New Taipei City Police Criminal Investigation Corps via Taiwan News

title: 17 Taiwanese indicted over Cebu scam base
detail: New Taipei prosecutors indicted 17 Taiwanese who ran a charity/romance scam base in Cebu from April 2024; 112 victims lost over NT$60 million; suspects deported from the Philippines in January 2026.
attribution: New Taipei District Prosecutors Office via Taipei Times

title: Fraud losses fall 26.9% in Q1 2026
detail: Justice Ministry said fraud losses in Q1 2026 fell 26.9% year on year and telecom fraud cases fell 9.1%.
attribution: Ministry of Justice via Taiwan News

title: China Coast Guard enters Kinmen waters twice in 24 hours
detail: CGA said four Chinese coast guard vessels entered Kinmen restricted waters around 3-5pm Tuesday and again 9-11am Wednesday (May 27), leaving after bilingual warnings.
attribution: Coast Guard Administration via Taiwan News

title: Taipei logs hottest May day on record, 38.3C
detail: CWA said Taipei station hit 38.3C, highest May reading since 1896; Tainan Yujing reached 39.8C and Xindian 39.6C.
attribution: Central Weather Administration via Taipei Times

title: Measles case linked to Thailand import; 491 contacts
detail: CDC reported a man in his 20s in northern Taiwan infected by an imported case from Thailand; 491 contacts self-monitoring to June 16.
attribution: Taiwan Centers for Disease Control via Taipei Times

title: 22 PLA aircraft, 8 warships tracked around Taiwan
detail: MND tracked 22 PLA aircraft, 8 naval vessels and 2 official ships in the 24 hours to 6am; two aircraft entered the central and southwestern ADIZ. June totals to date: 86 aircraft, 68 ships.
attribution: Ministry of National Defense via Taiwan News

title: Record 1,867kg ketamine haul from fishing boat
detail: CGA reported seizing 1,867.3kg of ketamine worth ~NT$3 billion from a fishing vessel at Donggang (seizure in January), the largest by weight involving a fishing vessel; boat owner and crew member arrested.
attribution: Coast Guard Administration via Taipei Times

title: Dengue cluster at Kaohsiung Min-Sheng Hospital
detail: CDC sent a mobile team after six local dengue (serotype 2) cases linked to Kaohsiung Municipal Min-Sheng Hospital; monitoring through July 12.
attribution: Taiwan Centers for Disease Control via Taipei Times

title: 304 live animals seized at Kinmen ferry terminal
detail: A traveller from Xiamen was caught with 304 live creatures including 208 geckos and beetles at Kinmen's mini-three-links terminal.
attribution: Kaohsiung Customs / Coast Guard Administration via Taipei Times

title: Taiwan announces five-day combat readiness exercise
detail: Taiwan's defence ministry announced a five-day exercise simulating a Chinese drill escalating into an attack, as it reported 21 Chinese aircraft operating nearby.
attribution: Ministry of National Defense via Semafor

title: New barrier lake forms on Wanli River after landslide
detail: FANCA Hualien Branch found a barrier lake after a 45-hectare landslide ~20km upstream of Wanrong; capacity est. 6 million m3, with as little as 1.5 million m3 enough to flood downstream. Precautionary evacuations urged.
attribution: Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency via Taipei Times

title: Carrier Fujian transits Taiwan Strait
detail: Stars and Stripes reported China's newest carrier Fujian passed through the Taiwan Strait, its first transit since December 2025, during Taiwan's Immediate Combat Readiness Exercise; MND said it monitored the movement.
attribution: Ministry of National Defense via Stars and Stripes

title: Tour bus and military minibus collide on Freeway 1
detail: 11 injured when a tour bus and military minibus collided on the southbound Yangmei elevated section in Guishan; minibus driver trapped.
attribution: Taoyuan City Fire Department via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: Heavy rain floods southern and northern Taiwan
detail: CWA attributed rain to Tropical Storm Mekkhala and a front; Pingtung logged 621mm, Kaohsiung 449.5mm, Tainan Nanhua 88mm in one hour; 10 residents stranded in Zhongkeng Village, bridges on Highway 20 closed.
attribution: Central Weather Administration via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: Wanli barrier lake overflow alert, 200 evacuated
detail: FANCA upgraded the alert warning the lake could overflow within 24 hours; about 200 residents of 70 households in seven villages of Wanrong and Fenglin evacuated and three bridges closed.
attribution: Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency via Taipei Times

title: Virtual Asset Services Act passed
detail: Legislature passed the Virtual Asset Services Act requiring FSC licensing of crypto service providers and 100% stablecoin reserves, with penalties of 3-10 years and NT$10-200 million fines.
attribution: Financial Supervisory Commission via The Crypto Times

title: Police bust US$300m World Cup betting ring in Tainan
detail: Police raided a house in Tainan used for illegal World Cup betting taking nearly NT$10 billion in wagers; 8 arrested, including 5 from Hong Kong and Macau.
attribution: Police via A News (AFP)

title: Red heat alert for Pingtung, orange for six areas
detail: CWA issued a red alert for Pingtung (38C for three days) and orange alerts for Tainan, Taipei, New Taipei, Kaohsiung, Yilan and Hualien.
attribution: Central Weather Administration via Taipei Times

title: Typhoon Bavi sea and land warnings
detail: CWA issued a sea warning at 2:30pm July 9 and land warning for July 10-11, forecasting 600-900mm in mountains; MND put 28,922 troops on standby.
attribution: Central Weather Administration via Taipei Times

title: Typhoon Bavi triggers landslide alerts and flooding
detail: 45 red landslide/debris-flow alerts and 214 stream debris-flow warnings were issued; flooding reported in Miaoli and landslides in mountain areas.
agency: Rural Development and Soil and Water Conservation Agency / CWA
attribution: Rural Development and Soil and Water Conservation Agency / CWA via Taipei Times

title: Typhoon Bavi injures 113, evacuates 14,605
detail: 113 injured (mostly motorcycle falls), no deaths; 14,605 evacuated led by Hualien 5,182; 2,156 damage reports.
attribution: Central Emergency Operation Center via Taipei Times

title: Bavi cuts power to 234,000 households
detail: 234,481 households lost power; 96% restored by 8pm, 8,126 still out, mainly Hsinchu and Taoyuan.
attribution: Taiwan Power Company via Taipei Times

title: Bavi grounds all domestic flights, 116 ferry sailings cut
detail: All domestic flights and international flights at Songshan, Taoyuan and Kaohsiung were cancelled; 116 sailings on 13 ferry routes including cross-strait services cancelled.
agency: Maritime and Port Bureau / aviation authorities
attribution: Maritime and Port Bureau / aviation authorities via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: PLA live-fire drills off Dongshan Island
detail: Zhangzhou Maritime Safety Administration declared live-fire zones off Dongshan, Fujian for July 23-24 (6am-6pm); Taiwan assessed them 57.6 nm from Kinmen and reported 19 PLA aircraft crossing the median line. Followed President Lai's DPP convention speech.
attribution: Zhangzhou Maritime Safety Administration (PRC) via The Epoch Times

title: M5.6 deep quake felt across northern Taiwan
detail: CWA recorded M5.6 at 8:36pm about 35.8km ESE of New Taipei City Hall at 95.7km depth; intensity 3 across north and central Taiwan; no damage reported.
attribution: Central Weather Administration via Taipei Times

title: Han Kuang 42 exercises begin
detail: The 42nd Han Kuang drills were scheduled for Aug 5-14, fully integrated with urban resilience civil exercises in Kaohsiung/Pingtung (Aug 6-7) and New Taipei/Yilan (Aug 12-13).
attribution: Ministry of National Defense via Taipei Times

title: Typhoon Dolphin suspends outlying-island ferries and flights
detail: Keelung-Matsu, Green Island and Orchid Island ferry routes suspended; EVA Air and Starlux cancelled Taiwan-Okinawa flights.
attribution: Maritime and Port Bureau via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: Sea warning for Typhoon Dolphin
detail: CWA issued a sea warning at 2:30pm for Typhoon Dolphin ~680km ENE of Taipei, max winds 144 kph, forecasting heavy rain in the north and central mountains.
attribution: Central Weather Administration via Taipei Times

title: PLA ADIZ air activity halves in 2026, naval presence steady
detail: Analysis of MND data: 1,200 PLA aircraft in Taiwan's ADIZ Jan 1-Aug 9, 2026 vs 2,501 in same period of 2025 (-52%); PLA Navy sightings 1,529 vs 1,647 (-7%).
attribution: Ministry of National Defense (data) via GlobalMilitary.net

title: China conducts seabed survey east of Taiwan
detail: China's Ministry of Natural Resources said it surveyed waters east of Taiwan Aug 10-31; Taiwan's coast guard condemned it as malicious harassment, saying China has no jurisdiction.
attribution: PRC Ministry of Natural Resources claim; CGA response, via Reuters/AsiaOne

title: NCC simulates mobile internet slowdowns in Han Kuang
detail: NCC scheduled simulated mobile internet slowdowns (2:30-3pm) in central Taiwan Aug 10 and northern Taiwan Aug 13 to test emergency communications.
attribution: National Communications Commission via Taipei Times

title: Foreign 'tourist' cash mules arrested in Kaohsiung
detail: Kaohsiung police arrested three Malaysians and one Hong Kong national who entered as tourists to withdraw scam proceeds from ATMs; all detained.
attribution: Kaohsiung Police Zuoying Precinct via Taipei Times

title: Two Chinese nationals held after rubber-boat landing
detail: Two Chinese nationals were detained after an abandoned rubber boat was found on a beach in Bali District; case referred to Shilin prosecutors; CGA apologised for detection failures.
attribution: Coast Guard Administration via Taipei Times

title: Over 20 arrested in scam targeting Taiwanese abroad
detail: Taipei police and CIB arrested 20+ suspects in a ring posing as investment advisers to Taiwanese and Chinese in the US, Japan and Canada; one California victim lost NT$89.26 million; funds moved via crypto to Taiwan, China or Cambodia.
agency: Taipei City Police / Criminal Investigation Bureau
attribution: Taipei City Police / Criminal Investigation Bureau via Taipei Times

title: Low-pressure rain floods southern and eastern Taiwan
detail: Over 400mm in 24h in Tainan's Yongkang and Rende; >4,000 evacuated; firefighters used boats to move ~200 people near An Nan Hospital; Eastern and South Link express trains suspended.
attribution: Water Resources Agency / local governments via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: Floods leave 1 dead, 4 missing, 155 injured
detail: Taipei Times reported 1 dead in Tainan, 4 missing (Tainan, Pingtung, Hualien) and 155 injured; Kaohsiung evacuated 2,649; Sanye River flooding closed Freeway 1 Rende interchange.
agency: Central Emergency Operation Center / local governments
attribution: Central Emergency Operation Center / local governments via Taipei Times

title: Wanli barrier lake level drops 4.7 m, 209 evacuated
detail: Heavy rain caused the Wanli River barrier lake to drop 4.7 metres and 209 residents were evacuated.
attribution: Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency via Taipei Times

title: Yuchang access road washed away; historic gate collapses
detail: Flooding washed away the temporary Yuchang access road linking Yuli and Changliang in Hualien; roads collapsed in Kaohsiung's Cianjhen, Renwu and Gangshan.
attribution: Local governments via Taipei Times

title: Eastern and South Link express trains suspended by floods
detail: Taiwan Railway Corp. suspended all express trains on the Eastern Line and South Link Line for the rest of Monday; road collapses in Kaohsiung.
attribution: Taiwan Railway Corporation via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: Wall of 1725 Great East Gate collapses in rain
detail: Part of the wall of Tainan's historic Great East Gate collapsed during flooding rains.
attribution: Tainan City Government via Taipei Times

title: Sea warning for Typhoon Saudel
detail: CWA issued a sea warning at 8:30am; Saudel was 560km ENE of Matsu with 126 kph winds; waves over 3m expected near Matsu, Lanyu and Green Island.
attribution: Central Weather Administration via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: 1,333 traffic deaths in first half of 2026
detail: MOTC reported 1,333 road deaths (30-day) in H1 2026, down 15% vs 2023 and 3.3% vs H1 2025; cyclist deaths rose 27.2% to 131.
attribution: Ministry of Transportation and Communications via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: Extremely heavy rain advisory for Pingtung as Saudel weakens
detail: CWA said Saudel weakened to a tropical storm; heavy rain advisories for Chiayi County, Tainan and Kaohsiung and extremely heavy rain advisory for Pingtung.
attribution: Central Weather Administration via Focus Taiwan (CNA)

title: CDC warns flu epidemic imminent
detail: CDC said Taiwan may enter a flu epidemic within 1-2 weeks: 101,628 flu-like visits last week, 85 severe cases and 14 deaths; H1N1 dominant.
attribution: Taiwan Centers for Disease Control via Taipei Times

title: 57 indicted over AI-powered romance scam
detail: Taipei prosecutors indicted 57 in a ring using AI voice-changing and fake dating profiles targeting 20,000+ people, with at least NT$900 million in proceeds.
attribution: Taipei District Prosecutors Office via Taipei Times

title: 34 indicted over farmland waste dumping
detail: Kaohsiung prosecutors indicted 34 people and 6 companies for dumping ~18,600m3 of construction waste on farmland in Daliao, with profits over NT$62 million.
attribution: Kaohsiung District Prosecutors Office via Taipei Times

title: 17 Chinese ships, 2 aircraft tracked
detail: MND tracked 13 PLA naval vessels, 4 official ships and 2 aircraft (both crossing the median line) in the 24 hours to 6am; September totals to date 26 aircraft and 69 ships.
attribution: Ministry of National Defense via Taiwan News

title: Four China Coast Guard ships intrude near Da Mao Shan, Kinmen
detail: CGA said four Chinese coast guard ships entered restricted waters southwest of Da Mao Shan in the morning and left two hours later after being shadowed and warned.
place: Southwest of Da Mao Shan, Kinmen
attribution: Coast Guard Administration via Taiwan News

title: Seven held in organ-trafficking recruitment ring
detail: CIB and Taoyuan prosecutors detained 7 who lured young people with fake job ads to a Jhongli residence, allegedly planning to send them abroad; one contacted organ buyers in China. Three victims held, none sent abroad.
agency: Criminal Investigation Bureau / Taoyuan District Prosecutors Office
attribution: Criminal Investigation Bureau / Taoyuan District Prosecutors Office via Taipei Times

title: Phishing cases double as overall fraud falls
detail: CIB said phishing cases rose to 505 with NT$54.51 million losses (vs 253 and NT$13.05 million a year earlier), while overall telecom/internet fraud fell 22.3% in cases and 35.1% in losses.
attribution: Criminal Investigation Bureau via Taipei Times
